entries.english:
June 1260, Hohenfurt. Wok von Rosenberg renews and increases the gifts made to his foundation at Hohenfurt.

In the name of the holy and indivisible Trinity, amen. Things done in time are perpetuated by witnesses and writing so that they do not pass away with time. We, Wok de Rosenberg, marshal of Bohemia, make known to all who see these presents that, with the consent and express will of our wife and all our relatives on both sides, inspired by divine grace, we have piously granted forever, with full right and without exception, the estates and revenues listed below to the Cistercian monastery at Hohenfurt, which we have begun to found and build anew in honor of Mary, the holy and perpetual virgin and mother of God, for the salvation and remedy of our soul and those of our ancestors and successors. We likewise establish the lawful boundaries of the grant.

The woodland on the other side of the Wulta reaches in its upper part to the road leading to Helfenberch, and in its lower part to the stream called the lesser Wultawitz, including the meadow Zbyadel, which must belong wholly to the monastery. Beginning at the Wulta, it extends upstream along the said stream to the height of the forest dividing Bohemia and Bavaria. On this side of the Wulta, beginning at the river itself, it runs upstream along a bank called Pzyn to a mountain called Strasedelnik and from there directly upwards across the boundaries of the villages of Zwatemyri to those of Herr Witigo de Krummenowe. We have also given the monastery fishing rights in the Wulta, beginning at the meadow Zbyadel and extending upstream to Witigo's boundary; nevertheless our own fishermen may fish there too.

The revenues we have given the monastery are: the church at Rosental with all its income and one third of the tithes from our villages and from others we have granted in fief in that parish, and the full tithes from our farm at Michenitz; the church at Predal with all income it can yield, the full tithes from our farm at Polen, and at Zlawatitz the full crop tithes from seven ploughlands, as well as tithes of cheese, lambs and everything else; the village of Cedelitz near Predal, which already belonged to the church there; the upper village of Gvtenprvnne near Strobnitz, with all its income; one third of our tithes from our village Levtwinitz and one third of the tithes from our village Plan.

We also acknowledge that we have given the monastery two vineyards, one given to us by the Graf de Hardekke and the other by our cousin Werenhard de Schowenberch der Jüngere; in the land of Opava, a newly founded and settled village called Kotzen, with all its income, in which fifty-two settlers now live; the portion of the tithe at Svnnenberch belonging to us; one third of the tithes from Stradonitz; the full tithes from our farm at Malschitz; a house site at Cedlikstrevt with the field belonging to it; and the village of Wawitz with all income it may yield.

To give the foregoing lasting force, we have had this document written and strengthened with our seal. The witnesses present are Herr Heinrich and Werenhard, brothers de Schowenberch; the younger brothers Werenhard and Heinrich of the same name; Herr Bvdewoy and his brother Herr Witigo de Krummenowe; Herr Poppo; Herr Hans; Herr Gerbert; Benata and Benisius, burgraves at Rosenberg; and many others. Done at Hohenfurt and written at Rosenberg in June of the year of grace 1260.

The white-wax seal, hanging from red silk, has now entirely crumbled. An extract appears in Millauer, p. 26.
